key: The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
s: In a surah on the night of revelation, between the sending down and the angels’ descent, the ayah weighs the night’s worth; al-Tabari, on 97:1 to 97:5, reads it as deeds done that night outweighing the deeds of a thousand months that lack it.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 97:1 to 97:5, the Tarteel QUL Arabic text via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: وأشبه الأقوال في ذلك بظاهر التنزيل قول من قال: عملٌ في ليلة القدر خير من عمل ألف شهر، ليس فيها ليلة القدر.
evidence.gloss: The view most in keeping with the plain wording of the revelation is that of those who said: deeds done on the Night of Power are better than the deeds of a thousand months in which there is no Night of Power.
evidence.licence: classical text public domain; digitisation by Tarteel (QUL), no licence stated; short excerpt with attribution

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Qadr 97:3, at 6127). In his single comment on 97:1 to 97:5 al-Tabari lists the readings (Mujahid and Amr ibn Qays: deeds that night; Qatada: months without the Night of Power; the Israelite warrior and Umayyad reports) and then states in his own voice that the reading closest to the plain wording is deeds on that night outweighing the deeds of a thousand months without it, dismissing the others. The sentence paraphrases exactly that. Plain sense places the ayah between the sending down (97:1) and the angels’ descent (97:4), faithful to day.js. 44 words; entry-check ok.
